case_analysis.thread_summary: The thread concerns scheduling and preparation for Bluetooth SIG RF qualification testing of a Bluetooth product. The customer and test laboratory coordinate quotation updates, required qualification documents, test setup information, shipping logistics, and laboratory scheduling constraints. A major issue arises when the laboratory’s Bluetooth RF test system requires periodic calibration, creating a conflict between the customer’s desired completion timing and available test capacity. The discussion ultimately focuses on whether testing can be completed in May using an overseas lab or deferred to early June using the domestic lab.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The technical discussion centers on RF-only Bluetooth qualification testing and confirmation of the product’s implemented Bluetooth functionality. The laboratory identifies a possible inconsistency between the submitted BR/EDR profile selections and the RF PHY procedures described in the test setup documentation, requiring clarification of the actual Bluetooth implementation scope. The parties discuss the need for questionnaires, test setup procedures, Bluetooth operation descriptions, antenna documentation, and compliance-related shipping paperwork required for overseas testing. The laboratory also explains that RF full-item testing requires calibrated InterLab equipment and that calibration downtime directly impacts available qualification schedules.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: The consultant’s reasoning is driven by qualification scope validation and test resource availability. Before scheduling testing, the consultant verifies whether the device is truly an RF-only implementation because this affects the applicable test scope and supporting documentation. The consultant also evaluates whether the customer can provide export-control documentation quickly enough to allow shipment to the Taiwan lab for earlier testing. When the required paperwork cannot be guaranteed in time, the consultant recommends domestic testing in June as the more realistic and lower-risk schedule.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: If the Bluetooth implementation scope is misunderstood, the wrong RF or profile-related test scope could be applied, potentially resulting in invalid qualification evidence or incomplete compliance coverage. If export-control documentation is delayed, overseas shipment cannot proceed, causing missed test windows and schedule slippage. Failure to coordinate test sample shipment timing with laboratory calibration schedules can also delay qualification completion by several weeks because RF test systems become temporarily unavailable during calibration.
case_analysis.consulting_mistake: The customer did not initially understand that periodic calibration downtime would affect laboratory availability and qualification timing. In parallel, the laboratory noted that earlier visibility into the desired qualification completion date and shipment schedule would have allowed better coordination before calibration equipment was sent overseas. The issue was corrected through clarification of schedule dependencies, calibration timing, and shipping/documentation requirements.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Bluetooth qualification consulting requires early alignment between implementation scope, required documentation, export logistics, and laboratory availability. Consultants should validate Bluetooth feature scope against ICS-related documentation before test scheduling and proactively identify dependencies such as calibration downtime, overseas shipment paperwork, and test sample readiness to avoid avoidable qualification delays.
